note_en: 既 A 又 B means "both A and B at once": 既 goes before the first quality, 又 before the second, and one is never used without the other. In the text: 她既兴奋又紧张 "she was both thrilled and nervous"; 房子不大，却既离地铁站近，又能看见远处的山 "the apartment wasn't big, but it was close to the subway and had a view of the distant hills"; 既离不开城市的机会，又放不下乡下的根 "she can't do without the city's opportunities, nor let go of her country roots." The halves can be short adjectives or whole verb phrases.
